predecessors.name: Chola Empire
predecessors.text: the Nellore district, where the Telugu Choda chiefs served the Imperial Cholas, Kakatiyas and Western Chalukyas ('chieftains to Imperial Cholas, Kakatiyas and Western Chalukyas', Nellore Chodas page)

successors.name: Kakatiya dynasty
successors.text: 'In 1290 CE, Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore' (Ambadeva page)

ledger.x: c. 1100: the Nellore Chodas appear as the south Andhra branch. 'nellore Chodas was the most predominant Chola branch who ruled south Andhra from 1100 to 1350 A.D.' The page gives the span, not a founding act; the land is the Nellore Chodas page's four districts with Vikramasimhapuri (Nellore) as capital.

c. 1100 (rounded start, as the found event): the Nellore Choda chiefs are Chola feudatories. Nellore Chodas page: they were 'chieftains to Imperial Cholas'; Ganapati page: 'Nalla-siddhi and his younger brother Tammu-siddhi ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208' and the Nellore Choda chiefs 'were Chola vassals'. The…
1208: the Chola hold on Nellore ends.

c. 1257: the Pandyas invade Nellore. 'Manumasiddhi, also known as Vira-gandagopala, the Telugu Chola ruler of Nellore... faced renewed pressure from the south following the invasion of Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I around c. 1257 CE.' The Ganapati page agrees ('around 1257'); the Nellore Chodas page says 1260.
1258: the Pandyas take Kanchipuram and kill Vijaya Gandagopala.
1263: the Kakatiya vassalage ends with the Pandya conquest.
1263: the fighting for Nellore ends at Muttukuru.
before 1281: Manuma Ganda-gopala regains the Nellore throne.
before 1281/1282: Manuma Ganda-gopala holds Nellore as Ambadeva's nominee.
1290: Ambadeva's hold on Nellore ends when 'Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore.'
1290: the Telugu Chodas of Nellore end with Manuma-Gandagopala's defeat.

wars.name: Pandya invasion of Nellore
wars.outcome: Pandya victory: Kanchipuram captured in 1258, Nellore in 1263 at Muttukuru, where Manuma-siddhi II was killed; his brothers ruled as Pandya vassals.

wars.name: Kakatiya campaign against Manuma-Gandagopala
wars.outcome: Kakatiya victory: Prataparudra defeats the Nellore ruler appointed by Amba-deva in 1290 and Nellore becomes Kakatiya land.

certainty.note: The pages name districts and cities, never a boundary; the Pandya-Kakatiya frontier around Nellore moved with each campaign (1257-1263, 1279-1290).
